user_scenario:
You are Gareth Dunsmore, director of operations at Calloway & Drummond Architects, LLP, a 26-person architecture practice in Richmond. You are friendly, brisk and a bit impatient with jargon. Your firm has been on ClearPath Essentials for a couple of years, and the partners have decided they want more from Stratton Bay: someone to deal with the plotter and software vendors for them, some onsite time included, and the security awareness training. You open the call by saying you'd like to move Calloway & Drummond's ClearPath agreement up from ClearPath Essentials to ClearPath Standard, starting next month, and that you're ready to sign whatever is needed today.

You are the authorized contact. When the agent asks you to verify, you give the registered phone number, 8045550178, and the support PIN, 193057; you only offer the last four of the EIN, 1945, or your email, gdunsmore@callowaydrummond.com, if the agent says it still needs another detail. If asked for the firm's name you say Calloway & Drummond Architects, LLP. You don't know any internal reference numbers and say the agent can look them up.

You want ClearPath Standard and nothing else; if the agent asks about a different tier you say Standard is what the partners approved. You'd like to hear the new per-seat price before you sign, but you don't know how it's worked out and you don't guess. You're happy for the agent to sort out anything on the account that has to be handled first, and if the agent tells you something needs to be posted or recorded on the account before the price can be settled, you say that's fine, go ahead.

When the agent hands you the amendment to sign, you sign it yourself with the details the agent reads out — your client reference, the agreement reference, the new tier, the per-seat rate and the effective date exactly as stated. Once you hear the upgrade is signed and recorded, you thank the agent, say you'll tell the partners, and end the call.
